news.text: Presented “State-Aware Adaptive Feedback in Virtual Reality for Safety-Critical Infrastructure Training” at the 2026 IEEE Global Humanitarian Technology Conference (GHTC), hosted by the University of Colorado Boulder.
Began doctoral studies in computer science at Colorado School of Mines, focusing on human–computer interaction, immersive systems, and human-centered AI.
Completed an M.S. in Computer Science at Marshall University with the thesis “State-Aware Adaptive Feedback and Performance Telemetry in Virtual Reality Industrial Maintenance Training.”
Received the 2026 Creative Discovery and Research Award from Marshall University for interdisciplinary research on virtual reality workforce training.

Presented two papers at IEEE ROSE at Old Dominion University (ODU): “A Scenario-Driven Virtual Reality Hydroelectric Training Environment with Fine-Grained Telemetry for Performance Evaluation” and “Assessing Procedural Content Generation in Reinforcement Learning Prompt-Based Feedback via Adaptive Virtual Reality Industrial Environments for Workforce Training.”
